job.prompt:
You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

printed-image-dimensions-v1
Read the ORIGINAL supplied drawing images for printed numeric engineering evidence.
For each requested page_N return state known and value_json a JSON array of objects
with EXACT keys text, token, value, unit, box. text copies the complete printed
dimension/callout context; token copies ONE literal printed numeric token from
that text; value is only that token parsed as a number (decimal comma is allowed).
unit is mm, deg, count, or unitless according to the printed context. Preserve
diameter/radius/depth/thread symbols and THRU/count qualifiers in text; do not
turn a thread nominal size into a bore, a radius into a diameter, or a tolerance
into a nominal dimension. Multiple numbers in one callout need separate entries
with the same full text and bounding box and their respective tokens/units.
Include printed overall/body dimensions, thickness alternatives, feature sizes,
hole/slot counts, pitches, offsets, diameters/radii, depths, angles and edge/corner
details. Ignore title-block weight, dates, drawing IDs, scale and page numbers.
Do not assign an unlabeled number to a geometric meaning at this stage. Do not
derive coordinates, scale/convert units, infer hardware dimensions, use another
drawing, or measure geometry from pixels. A box only LOCATES PRINTED TEXT.
box is [x,y,width,height] in ORIGINAL PDF page points, origin top left; convert
the text's image location using the supplied PDF page width/height. It must
tightly enclose the actual printed label/callout, not an entire view or page.
Do not invent unreadable characters. Include only confidently legible tokens.
Use known [] if that page has no legible engineering numbers; unreadable numbers
remain absent. This does not claim a complete drawing or approve any design.
Cite only the supplied drawing/source ID for each page item. In reason identify
which visible dimensions/callouts were readable and what remained unreadable.
The verifier must inspect EVERY token, copied context, unit and exact location
against that ORIGINAL page. Reject a guessed/changed token, wrong page, unrelated
box, inferred dimension or incorrectly classified unit. A close location can be
corrected in the one bounded retry; it never authorizes pixel measurements.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using
allow_primary_hole_without_unresolved_step=true, step_conflict_reason explaining the exact
printed conflict, and nonempty feature fact_ids. This flag is only for a supported through-hole whose
counterbore (or derived countersink depth) is invalid for at least one documented thickness variant.
The step dimensions and opening face must still be established. Explain the unresolved step in
features_omitted and set features_complete=false. CAD must skip that step per invalid variant and
report the omission; never clamp its depth, invent a face, silently replace it, or discard the valid
primary hole. Do not use this flag for an unsupported
primary hole or for missing primary-hole diameter/position.
features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
Each omission must cite exact supplied evidence IDs (the drawing/source ID may ground an image-only
feature) and explain precisely what is missing or why it cannot be modeled. Use [] only if nothing
is omitted. features_complete is a known JSON boolean: true ONLY when the entire visible feature
inventory is supported and features_omitted is []; false when any feature/detail is omitted. If the
inventory cannot be established, set features_complete unknown/null and explain the uncertainty in
features_omitted. Missing features never justify guessing or claiming the full design is verified.
All numeric scalar fields within a feature must be {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
A feature may carry parent fact_ids. Every numeric value must match its cited drawing number.
For an arithmetically derived coordinate/radius use {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs],
expression:'n0/2-n1'}, where n0,n1 are cited drawing numbers IN ORDER. Only +,-,*,/ and constants
0,1,2 are allowed. Do not invent absolute positions from undimensioned views. You may use literal
0 for a geometrically established center or literal 90/180/270/360 for cardinal pattern directions.
Do not infer numeric dimensions from pixels, scale, standard hardware, or undimensioned symmetry.
Conventional layout interpretation changes placement only; every numeric dimension/count and every
derived coordinate still requires the printed evidence and permitted arithmetic above.
Features must use same deterministic ordering: holes before slots, then x ascending, then y ascending.
Additional supported cuts: a hole in a rectangular body's side may use face x_min/x_max/y_min/y_max.
It still needs global entry x,y plus a sourced z numeric wrapper in the Z=0..thickness frame.
Its side-normal entry coordinate must equal that rectangle face boundary (+/-length/2 or +/-width/2),
using cited arithmetic. Its other coordinates, drill diameter, plain/threaded hole_type, through
boolean or blind depth must be established by the actual projected side/section views. A centered
z may use expression n0/2 from printed thickness ONLY when those views establish that centering;
do not assume side holes are centered merely to create a model. Side patterns and stepped side holes
are unsupported. No face changes are allowed just to make a top/bottom cut fit.
A dimensioned through-thickness rectangular outline corner clip may use
{kind:'corner_chamfer',corners:['x_min_y_min','x_min_y_max','x_max_y_min','x_max_y_max'],
x_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},
y_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},fact_ids:[IDs]}.
corners is only the nonempty unique subset actually established in the original views. This object

job.prompt:
You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using
allow_primary_hole_without_unresolved_step=true, step_conflict_reason explaining the exact
printed conflict, and nonempty feature fact_ids. This flag is only for a supported through-hole whose
counterbore (or derived countersink depth) is invalid for at least one documented thickness variant.
The step dimensions and opening face must still be established. Explain the unresolved step in
features_omitted and set features_complete=false. CAD must skip that step per invalid variant and
report the omission; never clamp its depth, invent a face, silently replace it, or discard the valid
primary hole. Do not use this flag for an unsupported
primary hole or for missing primary-hole diameter/position.
features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
Each omission must cite exact supplied evidence IDs (the drawing/source ID may ground an image-only
feature) and explain precisely what is missing or why it cannot be modeled. Use [] only if nothing
is omitted. features_complete is a known JSON boolean: true ONLY when the entire visible feature
inventory is supported and features_omitted is []; false when any feature/detail is omitted. If the
inventory cannot be established, set features_complete unknown/null and explain the uncertainty in
features_omitted. Missing features never justify guessing or claiming the full design is verified.
All numeric scalar fields within a feature must be {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
A feature may carry parent fact_ids. Every numeric value must match its cited drawing number.
For an arithmetically derived coordinate/radius use {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs],
expression:'n0/2-n1'}, where n0,n1 are cited drawing numbers IN ORDER. Only +,-,*,/ and constants
0,1,2 are allowed. Do not invent absolute positions from undimensioned views. You may use literal
0 for a geometrically established center or literal 90/180/270/360 for cardinal pattern directions.
Do not infer numeric dimensions from pixels, scale, standard hardware, or undimensioned symmetry.
Conventional layout interpretation changes placement only; every numeric dimension/count and every
derived coordinate still requires the printed evidence and permitted arithmetic above.
Features must use same deterministic ordering: holes before slots, then x ascending, then y ascending.
Additional supported cuts: a hole in a rectangular body's side may use face x_min/x_max/y_min/y_max.
It still needs global entry x,y plus a sourced z numeric wrapper in the Z=0..thickness frame.
Its side-normal entry coordinate must equal that rectangle face boundary (+/-length/2 or +/-width/2),
using cited arithmetic. Its other coordinates, drill diameter, plain/threaded hole_type, through
boolean or blind depth must be established by the actual projected side/section views. A centered
z may use expression n0/2 from printed thickness ONLY when those views establish that centering;
do not assume side holes are centered merely to create a model. Side patterns and stepped side holes
are unsupported. No face changes are allowed just to make a top/bottom cut fit.
A dimensioned through-thickness rectangular outline corner clip may use
{kind:'corner_chamfer',corners:['x_min_y_min','x_min_y_max','x_max_y_min','x_max_y_max'],
x_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},
y_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},fact_ids:[IDs]}.
corners is only the nonempty unique subset actually established in the original views. This object
has no face/x/y/through or pattern. Both setbacks must be independently printed or equal setbacks
explicitly established by a 45-degree chamfer callout. Never treat an arbitrary rounded/stepped
outline as corner clips, infer setback from pixels, or assume every corner shares a lone callout.
Use corner_chamfer only for straight through-thickness outline clips, not surface edge bevels.

ADDITIONAL MVP ELIGIBILITY CHECK (mandatory, independent of dimension readings):
Return the extra requested key cad_eligibility, state known, value_json an object
with EXACT keys: supported (boolean), constant_thickness (boolean), outline_exact
(boolean), reason (nonempty string), essential_uncertainty (array of strings),
omitted_minor_features (array of strings). Cite original drawing source IDs.
supported=true only when the main body can be represented by the supported
rectangle/circle/ring outline, a single constant thickness (or explicitly printed
alternative constant thicknesses), plus supported hole/slot cuts, source-dimensioned
plain/threaded side holes and explicit full-thickness rectangular-corner chamfers.
Known corner clips are represented by corner_chamfer features, never silently
discarded. The MAIN
outline must match exactly: do not substitute its bounding rectangle or circle.
Block bent, stepped, revolved, profiled, tapered, nonplanar or assembled parts and
essential notches, lobes, rounded outer corners or other contours the generator
cannot express. Do not classify an essential contour as an omitted minor detail.
Small undimensioned corner chamfers and edge breaks may be explicitly omitted
from an otherwise dimensioned rectangular plate, as in the original MVP flat-part
models. In that case outline_exact refers to the established main rectangular
body dimensions, not a claim that the omitted corner detail has been reproduced.
Do not use this allowance for a functional contour, large corner cut, missing
overall dimension, rounded profile, or a bounding box around another shape.
Do not infer a constant thickness from an unlabeled number, another part, title,
material, stock convention, scale, pixels, or a familiar standard. Printed numbers
must be linked by the actual view/dimension leaders to the dimension claimed;
detached text and unrelated numbers are not dimension evidence. All numeric
geometry must cite exact supplied parsed or separately verified image-dimension
IDs; verified image dimensions are AI evidence, not deterministic PDF text. The original image
can establish their meaning, but never invent missing numbers or evidence IDs.
If dimensions are absent/unreadable, keep them unknown. Explain which essential
dimension/contour is unresolved. A certain outline and thickness can still produce
an honest partial model when minor holes/slots lack positions or dimensions:
list the omissions, retain only fully supported features, and do not guess them.
Uncertainty about a minor hole alone MUST NOT block the main constant-thickness
solid. For such partials features remains known with the supported subset,
features_complete is false, and features_omitted describes every excluded detail
with original evidence IDs. Do not erase supported cuts because another feature
is unresolved. Minor unsupported cut orientations may be explicitly omitted, but
unsupported essential functional features must be reported as a reason for a
partial or blocked reconstruction. A blank body is never evidence that the
functional part has been reconstructed accurately. The object reason must explain
the specific eligibility decision, including the main view and thickness source.
Do not consult prior AI records, fused application records, existing templates,
benchmark expectations, accepted human decisions, or any other drawings.


DETAIL-FIDELITY PASS: inspect EVERY original view, section, detail, leader and
functional note. Enumerate through and blind holes, side-drilled holes, stepped
holes/counterbores, countersinks, recesses, slots, notches, corner chamfers,
grooves and indents before deciding which supported features to emit. Inspect
the original evidence afresh, not an earlier template or reconstruction.
Never omit an expressible fully dimensioned feature merely because the primary
outline is easy to generate. Use all relevant supplied parsed AND verified image
dimension IDs. Image-only readings remain AI evidence with their own receipts.
Check each feature's axis, opening face, size, depth, count, and complete location.
An unspecified edge break is not permission to add an arbitrary chamfer. Missing
pitch/coordinates are not permission to measure pixels or assume symmetry.
Describe EACH genuinely unsupported or undimensioned detail in features_omitted,
distinguishing a missing source dimension from a generator limitation. Preserve
all independently supported cuts. Do not label a partial reconstruction complete.

omitted_minor_features (array of strings). Cite original drawing source IDs.
supported=true only when the main body can be represented by the supported
rectangle/circle/ring outline, a single constant thickness (or explicitly printed
alternative constant thicknesses), plus supported hole/slot cuts, source-dimensioned
plain/threaded side holes and explicit full-thickness rectangular-corner chamfers.
Known corner clips are represented by corner_chamfer features, never silently
discarded. The MAIN
outline must match exactly: do not substitute its bounding rectangle or circle.
Block bent, stepped, revolved, profiled, tapered, nonplanar or assembled parts and
essential notches, lobes, rounded outer corners or other contours the generator
cannot express. Do not classify an essential contour as an omitted minor detail.
Small undimensioned corner chamfers and edge breaks may be explicitly omitted
from an otherwise dimensioned rectangular plate, as in the original MVP flat-part
models. In that case outline_exact refers to the established main rectangular
body dimensions, not a claim that the omitted corner detail has been reproduced.
Do not use this allowance for a functional contour, large corner cut, missing
overall dimension, rounded profile, or a bounding box around another shape.
Do not infer a constant thickness from an unlabeled number, another part, title,
material, stock convention, scale, pixels, or a familiar standard. Printed numbers
must be linked by the actual view/dimension leaders to the dimension claimed;
detached text and unrelated numbers are not dimension evidence. All numeric
geometry must cite exact supplied parsed or separately verified image-dimension
IDs; verified image dimensions are AI evidence, not deterministic PDF text. The original image
can establish their meaning, but never invent missing numbers or evidence IDs.
If dimensions are absent/unreadable, keep them unknown. Explain which essential
dimension/contour is unresolved. A certain outline and thickness can still produce
an honest partial model when minor holes/slots lack positions or dimensions:
list the omissions, retain only fully supported features, and do not guess them.

features_complete is false, and features_omitted describes every excluded detail
with original evidence IDs. Do not erase supported cuts because another feature

functional part has been reconstructed accurately. The object reason must explain
the specific eligibility decision, including the main view and thickness source.
Do not consult prior AI records, fused application records, existing templates,
benchmark expectations, accepted human decisions, or any other drawings.

all independently supported cuts. Do not label a partial reconstruction complete.

You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.

You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using

features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.

corners is only the nonempty unique subset actually established in the original views. This object

The main face-on view in D-005 shows a rectangular frame with large rounded outer corners, and no outer corner radius is printed. That outline is not an exact rectangle, circle or ring, so the proposed unknown is correct. Because this is essential geometry, the verdict is needs_input. A rectangle cannot be chosen without substituting the bounding box.
In the main view, 323,0 is the horizontal overall dimension. Its extension lines run to the outer left and right extents of the frame.
In the main view, 236,0 is the vertical overall dimension on the right side. Its extension lines run to the outer top and bottom extents.
The outline is not circular and no outer diameter is printed. Leaving this not-applicable field unknown is correct.
The window opening is a rounded rectangle measuring 286,7 by 199,7, not a circle, and no inner diameter is printed. Unknown is correct.

In the left side view, 8,2 is dimensioned between extension lines across the full face-to-face depth, so it is the overall thickness. The reason correctly says this does not show uniform local thickness, since Section A-A and Detail B show a stepped profile.

The 20 holes are visible in the main view as 5 per side. The callout gives their count, drill diameter, thread and depths, but no pitch, offset or center coordinates are printed, and the opening face is not separately established. The window opening, seat and grooves are not supported hole or slot cuts. No cut is fully supported, so known [] is correct.
Several visible features are omitted, including the opening, seat, two grooves, 20 tapped holes, rounded corners, machining relief and the 3,0 X 45° bevel. Therefore false is correct.

Each omission matches the drawing. Rounded outer corners have no radius. The window opening's extents are 286,7 by 199,7, but its corner radii are not given. The 297,2 by 210,2 seat is shown stepped in Section A-A and Detail B, but its depth and corner geometry are incomplete. In Detail B, the 2,0 and 3,3 groove dimensions and the maximum 0.5 mm bottom-corner radius note are shown, but the groove paths are not dimensioned. The tapped holes have the callout 20 x Ø3,3 ↧6,0 / M4-6H ↧4,0 but no center dimensions. The machining-relief leader says 'Resize as needed' and gives no dimensions. The 3,0 X 45° callout is a side-view edge bevel. The deburr note has no size. Each citation is an exact source ID.

The proposal sets supported=false, outline_exact=false and constant_thickness=false. The drawing supports all three. The main view establishes a rounded-corner frame of 323,0 by 236,0 with no corner radii. The 8,2 side-view dimension is the overall depth, while Section A-A and Detail B show a stepped seat and grooved section, so the body is not a constant-thickness flat plate. These essential contours cannot be expressed by the template, and a bounding blank would misrepresent the part.

job.prompt:
You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using
allow_primary_hole_without_unresolved_step=true, step_conflict_reason explaining the exact
printed conflict, and nonempty feature fact_ids. This flag is only for a supported through-hole whose
counterbore (or derived countersink depth) is invalid for at least one documented thickness variant.
The step dimensions and opening face must still be established. Explain the unresolved step in
features_omitted and set features_complete=false. CAD must skip that step per invalid variant and
report the omission; never clamp its depth, invent a face, silently replace it, or discard the valid
primary hole. Do not use this flag for an unsupported
primary hole or for missing primary-hole diameter/position.
features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
Each omission must cite exact supplied evidence IDs (the drawing/source ID may ground an image-only
feature) and explain precisely what is missing or why it cannot be modeled. Use [] only if nothing
is omitted. features_complete is a known JSON boolean: true ONLY when the entire visible feature
inventory is supported and features_omitted is []; false when any feature/detail is omitted. If the
inventory cannot be established, set features_complete unknown/null and explain the uncertainty in
features_omitted. Missing features never justify guessing or claiming the full design is verified.
All numeric scalar fields within a feature must be {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
A feature may carry parent fact_ids. Every numeric value must match its cited drawing number.
For an arithmetically derived coordinate/radius use {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs],
expression:'n0/2-n1'}, where n0,n1 are cited drawing numbers IN ORDER. Only +,-,*,/ and constants
0,1,2 are allowed. Do not invent absolute positions from undimensioned views. You may use literal
0 for a geometrically established center or literal 90/180/270/360 for cardinal pattern directions.
Do not infer numeric dimensions from pixels, scale, standard hardware, or undimensioned symmetry.
Conventional layout interpretation changes placement only; every numeric dimension/count and every
derived coordinate still requires the printed evidence and permitted arithmetic above.
Features must use same deterministic ordering: holes before slots, then x ascending, then y ascending.
Additional supported cuts: a hole in a rectangular body's side may use face x_min/x_max/y_min/y_max.
It still needs global entry x,y plus a sourced z numeric wrapper in the Z=0..thickness frame.
Its side-normal entry coordinate must equal that rectangle face boundary (+/-length/2 or +/-width/2),
using cited arithmetic. Its other coordinates, drill diameter, plain/threaded hole_type, through
boolean or blind depth must be established by the actual projected side/section views. A centered
z may use expression n0/2 from printed thickness ONLY when those views establish that centering;
do not assume side holes are centered merely to create a model. Side patterns and stepped side holes
are unsupported. No face changes are allowed just to make a top/bottom cut fit.
A dimensioned through-thickness rectangular outline corner clip may use
{kind:'corner_chamfer',corners:['x_min_y_min','x_min_y_max','x_max_y_min','x_max_y_max'],
x_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},
y_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},fact_ids:[IDs]}.
corners is only the nonempty unique subset actually established in the original views. This object
has no face/x/y/through or pattern. Both setbacks must be independently printed or equal setbacks
explicitly established by a 45-degree chamfer callout. Never treat an arbitrary rounded/stepped
outline as corner clips, infer setback from pixels, or assume every corner shares a lone callout.
Use corner_chamfer only for straight through-thickness outline clips, not surface edge bevels.

job.prompt:
You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using
allow_primary_hole_without_unresolved_step=true, step_conflict_reason explaining the exact
printed conflict, and nonempty feature fact_ids. This flag is only for a supported through-hole whose
counterbore (or derived countersink depth) is invalid for at least one documented thickness variant.
The step dimensions and opening face must still be established. Explain the unresolved step in
features_omitted and set features_complete=false. CAD must skip that step per invalid variant and
report the omission; never clamp its depth, invent a face, silently replace it, or discard the valid
primary hole. Do not use this flag for an unsupported
primary hole or for missing primary-hole diameter/position.
features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
Each omission must cite exact supplied evidence IDs (the drawing/source ID may ground an image-only
feature) and explain precisely what is missing or why it cannot be modeled. Use [] only if nothing
is omitted. features_complete is a known JSON boolean: true ONLY when the entire visible feature
inventory is supported and features_omitted is []; false when any feature/detail is omitted. If the
inventory cannot be established, set features_complete unknown/null and explain the uncertainty in
features_omitted. Missing features never justify guessing or claiming the full design is verified.
All numeric scalar fields within a feature must be {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]}.

job.prompt:
You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout
establish a row, circle, or mirrored layout. A circle distributes its printed count using 360/count;
rows and mirrored positions derive from the printed pitch/offset and count. This is an AI layout
interpretation, not a claim that every coordinate or angle is explicitly printed or human approved.
Tag each feature placement_basis='dimensioned' when directly dimensioned, otherwise
placement_basis='drawing_pattern_interpretation' with nonempty placement_reason explaining the exact
printed dimensions/count, axes/layout and derivation, plus nonempty feature fact_ids citing exact
source IDs. Opus must verify this EXACT layout against the original views; ambiguous layouts require
reject/needs_input and an omission, never arbitrary symmetry or an inferred bolt-circle dimension.
features is the independently supported SUBSET of cuts, not a
claim that every drawing feature is determined. Return features state known with all and ONLY cuts
whose geometry, position, and operation are fully supported, even when other features are unresolved.
Use known [] when no cuts can be supported; do not erase supported cuts because another is uncertain.
Never fabricate a drill diameter, depth, position, or count to complete a cut. A feature missing any
required geometry must be excluded from features and described separately in features_omitted.
Exception for a documented counterbore-step/thickness-variant conflict: preserve the separately
printed primary through-hole and actual counterbore dimensions in one counterbored feature using
allow_primary_hole_without_unresolved_step=true, step_conflict_reason explaining the exact
printed conflict, and nonempty feature fact_ids. This flag is only for a supported through-hole whose
counterbore (or derived countersink depth) is invalid for at least one documented thickness variant.
The step dimensions and opening face must still be established. Explain the unresolved step in
features_omitted and set features_complete=false. CAD must skip that step per invalid variant and
report the omission; never clamp its depth, invent a face, silently replace it, or discard the valid
primary hole. Do not use this flag for an unsupported
primary hole or for missing primary-hole diameter/position.
features_omitted is a known JSON array of {description:string,reason:string,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
Each omission must cite exact supplied evidence IDs (the drawing/source ID may ground an image-only
feature) and explain precisely what is missing or why it cannot be modeled. Use [] only if nothing
is omitted. features_complete is a known JSON boolean: true ONLY when the entire visible feature
inventory is supported and features_omitted is []; false when any feature/detail is omitted. If the
inventory cannot be established, set features_complete unknown/null and explain the uncertainty in
features_omitted. Missing features never justify guessing or claiming the full design is verified.
All numeric scalar fields within a feature must be {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]}.
A feature may carry parent fact_ids. Every numeric value must match its cited drawing number.
For an arithmetically derived coordinate/radius use {state:known,value:number,fact_ids:[IDs],
expression:'n0/2-n1'}, where n0,n1 are cited drawing numbers IN ORDER. Only +,-,*,/ and constants
0,1,2 are allowed. Do not invent absolute positions from undimensioned views. You may use literal
0 for a geometrically established center or literal 90/180/270/360 for cardinal pattern directions.
Do not infer numeric dimensions from pixels, scale, standard hardware, or undimensioned symmetry.
Conventional layout interpretation changes placement only; every numeric dimension/count and every
derived coordinate still requires the printed evidence and permitted arithmetic above.
Features must use same deterministic ordering: holes before slots, then x ascending, then y ascending.
Additional supported cuts: a hole in a rectangular body's side may use face x_min/x_max/y_min/y_max.
It still needs global entry x,y plus a sourced z numeric wrapper in the Z=0..thickness frame.
Its side-normal entry coordinate must equal that rectangle face boundary (+/-length/2 or +/-width/2),
using cited arithmetic. Its other coordinates, drill diameter, plain/threaded hole_type, through
boolean or blind depth must be established by the actual projected side/section views. A centered
z may use expression n0/2 from printed thickness ONLY when those views establish that centering;
do not assume side holes are centered merely to create a model. Side patterns and stepped side holes
are unsupported. No face changes are allowed just to make a top/bottom cut fit.
A dimensioned through-thickness rectangular outline corner clip may use
{kind:'corner_chamfer',corners:['x_min_y_min','x_min_y_max','x_max_y_min','x_max_y_max'],
x_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},
y_setback:{state:'known',value:number,fact_ids:[IDs]},fact_ids:[IDs]}.
corners is only the nonempty unique subset actually established in the original views. This object
has no face/x/y/through or pattern. Both setbacks must be independently printed or equal setbacks
explicitly established by a 45-degree chamfer callout. Never treat an arbitrary rounded/stepped
outline as corner clips, infer setback from pixels, or assume every corner shares a lone callout.
Use corner_chamfer only for straight through-thickness outline clips, not surface edge bevels.

You are a read-only engineering evidence proposer. Do not edit files,
run commands, use other agents, browse the web, or inspect any evidence beyond the supplied inputs.
Return the requested JSON schema. Every requested key must appear exactly once. value_json is a
JSON-encoded value (e.g. a string as "\"text\"", a number as "5", an array as "[3,6]",
unknown as "null"). State known means one determined value; options means genuinely documented
alternatives; unknown means the evidence does not determine it. confidence is only sure or unsure.
Use sure only for a reading supported by the supplied evidence. Copy original spelling and units.
Never invent evidence IDs. fact_ids must be exact supplied source IDs supporting that item.
Reasons must explain the evidence; changed_because is empty on the first proposal.

Fill a flat-part template from this drawing, in millimetres.
Read the attached full drawing. The main material field and weight are supplied separately.
Requested keys: outline_type (rectangle/circle/ring), length (X), width (Y), outer_diameter,
inner_diameter, thickness, features, features_complete, features_omitted.
Feature protocol: supported-feature-subset-v1. Only relevant dimensions are known; irrelevant ones are unknown.
Stacked thickness values which are alternatives MUST be state options with a JSON array, sorted ascending.
Do not select one thickness or invent which example is primary. The outline is centered on X=0,Y=0;
extrusion Z=0..thickness. Use the main face-on outline drawing view as XY, viewed from +Z toward
the origin, with X right and Y up. top is Z=thickness, toward that viewer; bottom is Z=0, opposite.
Keep every feature position in this same XY frame, including bottom features. Verify which face a
countersink/counterbore opens from using the side, section, isometric, datum and projection evidence;
do not silently force steps onto top. If the opening face genuinely cannot be established, omit that
step with its uncertainty; retain a separately supported primary through-hole as plain only when its
diameter and placement are independently established. Ignore dimension text placement when interpreting actual geometry.
features value is a JSON array of hole/slot objects. Each has kind, face='top' or 'bottom', x,y,
diameter (hole) or width,length,direction (slot), through boolean, depth for blind holes,
hole_type plain/threaded/countersunk/counterbored, optional thread string and required actual
countersink_diameter/angle or counterbore_diameter/depth. Never infer a drill diameter from a thread.
Every slot MUST include a structured direction for its LONG axis in the main XY frame, measured in
degrees counterclockwise from +X. Use a known numeric wrapper with exact evidence IDs and permitted
arithmetic, or a canonical lowercase named axis: x/horizontal or y/vertical. The legacy angle alias
is accepted, but prefer direction. Cardinal 0/90/180/270/360 orientations may follow established
drawing axes; arbitrary angles need cited printed numeric evidence or permitted derivation. Prose
such as 'long axes follow Y' in placement_reason does NOT replace the structured direction field.
If slot orientation is genuinely unresolved, omit that slot with its reason rather than guessing.
Use explicit pattern only if certain: {type:row,count,spacing,direction} (angle degrees, anchor first
position) or {type:circle,count,radius,start_angle} (degrees, center x,y). Hole positions are center
coordinates in the same XY frame. Conventional drawing-pattern interpretation is allowed when a
printed count plus printed pitch, offset, radius or pitch-circle diameter AND clear axes/layout

ADDITIONAL MVP ELIGIBILITY CHECK (mandatory, independent of dimension readings):
Return the extra requested key cad_eligibility, state known, value_json an object
with EXACT keys: supported (boolean), constant_thickness (boolean), outline_exact
(boolean), reason (nonempty string), essential_uncertainty (array of strings),
omitted_minor_features (array of strings). Cite original drawing source IDs.
supported=true only when the main body can be represented by the supported
rectangle/circle/ring outline, a single constant thickness (or explicitly printed
alternative constant thicknesses), plus supported hole/slot cuts, source-dimensioned
plain/threaded side holes and explicit full-thickness rectangular-corner chamfers.
Known corner clips are represented by corner_chamfer features, never silently
discarded. The MAIN
outline must match exactly: do not substitute its bounding rectangle or circle.
Block bent, stepped, revolved, profiled, tapered, nonplanar or assembled parts and
essential notches, lobes, rounded outer corners or other contours the generator
cannot express. Do not classify an essential contour as an omitted minor detail.
Small undimensioned corner chamfers and edge breaks may be explicitly omitted
from an otherwise dimensioned rectangular plate, as in the original MVP flat-part
models. In that case outline_exact refers to the established main rectangular
body dimensions, not a claim that the omitted corner detail has been reproduced.
Do not use this allowance for a functional contour, large corner cut, missing
overall dimension, rounded profile, or a bounding box around another shape.
Do not infer a constant thickness from an unlabeled number, another part, title,
material, stock convention, scale, pixels, or a familiar standard. Printed numbers
must be linked by the actual view/dimension leaders to the dimension claimed;
detached text and unrelated numbers are not dimension evidence. All numeric
geometry must cite exact supplied parsed or separately verified image-dimension
IDs; verified image dimensions are AI evidence, not deterministic PDF text. The original image
can establish their meaning, but never invent missing numbers or evidence IDs.
If dimensions are absent/unreadable, keep them unknown. Explain which essential
dimension/contour is unresolved. A certain outline and thickness can still produce
an honest partial model when minor holes/slots lack positions or dimensions:
list the omissions, retain only fully supported features, and do not guess them.
Uncertainty about a minor hole alone MUST NOT block the main constant-thickness
solid. For such partials features remains known with the supported subset,
features_complete is false, and features_omitted describes every excluded detail
with original evidence IDs. Do not erase supported cuts because another feature
is unresolved. Minor unsupported cut orientations may be explicitly omitted, but
unsupported essential functional features must be reported as a reason for a
partial or blocked reconstruction. A blank body is never evidence that the
functional part has been reconstructed accurately. The object reason must explain
the specific eligibility decision, including the main view and thickness source.
Do not consult prior AI records, fused application records, existing templates,
benchmark expectations, accepted human decisions, or any other drawings.


DETAIL-FIDELITY PASS: inspect EVERY original view, section, detail, leader and
functional note. Enumerate through and blind holes, side-drilled holes, stepped
holes/counterbores, countersinks, recesses, slots, notches, corner chamfers,
grooves and indents before deciding which supported features to emit. Inspect
the original evidence afresh, not an earlier template or reconstruction.
Never omit an expressible fully dimensioned feature merely because the primary
outline is easy to generate. Use all relevant supplied parsed AND verified image
dimension IDs. Image-only readings remain AI evidence with their own receipts.
Check each feature's axis, opening face, size, depth, count, and complete location.
An unspecified edge break is not permission to add an arbitrary chamfer. Missing
pitch/coordinates are not permission to measure pixels or assume symmetry.
Describe EACH genuinely unsupported or undimensioned detail in features_omitted,
distinguishing a missing source dimension from a generator limitation. Preserve
all independently supported cuts. Do not label a partial reconstruction complete.
